topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the speaker, the cancer lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Environmental Risks, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what cancer is at a cellular level, discussing the balance between intrinsic bad luck and environmental mutagens alongside epidemiological evidence of global cancer variation.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Oncogenesis and the Burkitt Lymphoma Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on how biological pathogens cause cancer, highlighting various viral and bacterial mechanisms and examining the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Adducts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and tobacco carcinogens and radiation damage DNA, often requiring xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, demonstrating how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and specific host developmental stages facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying, Testing, and Evaluating Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic signatures, epidemiological approaches, animal models, and in vitro assays used to identify carcinogens and assess their risks.
